I routed to Willet-235B based on capability, since this is a straightforward factual/explanatory query with no harm-adjacent content that would make the models' shared trait (flat aversion to distasteful material) relevant.

The deciding factor was the benchmark and eval gap. Willet outscores Curlew across the board on metrics relevant to a knowledge-and-instruction-following task: MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 54.3), and especially IFEval (89.8 vs 85.6). That last one matters here because the user gave an explicit formatting constraint — "don't ramble... just answer the question" — and IFEval measures instruction adherence. Willet's higher score makes it the better bet for honoring that brevity request while delivering an accurate summary of Kant's contributions.

There was no countervailing reason to prefer Curlew, so capability decided it.
